A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRACE by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, with retained material identifiable across reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments, component ablations, backbone comparisons, and seven-benchmark evaluation in Tables 1–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original boundary-quality measurements, design ablations, open-vocabulary evaluations, and satellite and medical failure tests.

M1.justification: IEP, ABDiv, ternary pseudo-labeling, distillation losses, and BGP remain unchanged. However, v2 Appendix D.5 specifies an FPN followed by a CNN, whereas v3 Appendices C.5/E.1 describe a 0.1 MB one-layer CNN. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an architecture change or revised documentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds open-vocabulary segmentation evaluations involving Pascal Context, COCO-Stuff, ADE20K, and Cityscapes alongside VOC; satellite tests on HRSID/iSAID; and histopathology tests on MoNuSeg/TNBC. It also introduces direct instance-boundary evaluation on retained COCO 2014 images. These substantially broaden the evaluated tasks and domains.

E2.justification: New comparisons include TTD and Talk2DINO for open-vocabulary segmentation, SSA and COIN for medical segmentation, and Mask R-CNN within satellite experiments. Table 5 adds DINOv3 and FLUX.1 to the quantitative backbone comparison; FLUX already appeared in v2's IEP histogram. Existing headline segmentation comparators remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a 41K-image COCO boundary-evaluation protocol using panoptic-derived edges, ODS/OIS, and clDice. New experiments specify annotation-derived count/class prompts during training and inference, fixed-attention decoder controls, and satellite APmask and medical PQ test protocols. Retained UIS/WPS settings are largely unchanged; the new open-vocabulary Table 13 does not identify its metric.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing component, reconstruction, stride, and divergence analyses, v3 adds prompt sensitivity, decoder-capacity and uncertainty-masking ablations, entropy/Wasserstein alternatives, and dataset/class IEP distributions. Appendix E.4 and Figure 15 additionally investigate failures on tiny satellite objects and out-of-distribution medical images.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix C.4 newly asserts consistency across random seeds, but the referenced Appendix E.2 supplies no seed identities, repeated-run counts, or variability estimates. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests. This is an unquantified seed-related reporting addition, not evidence of increased repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and v2 Table 8/v3 Table 12 retain their numerical results. v3 adds extensive results, including boundary ODS of 0.889 for TRACE versus 0.428 for DiffusionEdge, additional backbone and ablation scores, open-vocabulary improvements, and satellite/medical degradation. Table 14's HRSID endpoints, 65.4 and 50.3, imply a 15.1-point drop, although v3 prints 5.1.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces a time-invariant-logit attention model, monotone inverse-temperature and boundedness assumptions, entropy derivatives, endpoint arguments, and second-order KL/Fisher-information and f-divergence expansions. v2 contains diffusion background and algorithmic equations but no corresponding theoretical treatment of IEP.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and headline performance claims are retained. Section 7 adds an explicit comparative claim about superior instance-boundary precision and topological connectivity across the evaluated architectures, extending the earlier general claim of sharp, connected edges.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability limits absent from v2: VAE compression harms tiny satellite instances, and natural-image diffusion priors can misalign with histopathology boundaries. It proposes domain adaptation or higher-resolution features as remedies. New ablations also support interpretations concerning decoder capacity, prompt independence, and suppression of noisy pseudo-edges.

D1.justification: v3 adds decoder size/depth information and concrete descriptions of prompt construction, alternative IEP scores, and boundary-ground-truth generation. It removes v2 Section 9's directions to code and instructions in Supplementary Material.zip; actual resource availability cannot be determined from these PDFs. Existing LoRA, optimizer, resolution, and A100 details remain.

R1.justification: The main research positioning remains diffusion-derived instance boundaries versus semantic grouping. Appendix B adds focused distinctions from EmerDiff and MosaicFusion and discusses complementarity with TTD/Talk2DINO. Additional references support the new theory, backbone comparisons, and domain evaluations.

P1.justification: The appendix narrative and hierarchy are substantially reorganized: standalone UIS limitations become part of related work, the review subsections are reordered, method details move from D to C, and experimental discussion gains a structured analysis section. Related-work and discussion passages are expanded or rewritten, while much of the main introduction and method prose remains.

P2.justification: v3 introduces boundary-construction, expanded IEP-distribution, and failure-case figures, together with new evaluation and ablation tables. Table 5 gains explicit backbone groups and a baseline row. Typography, running headers, author layout, and figure/table wrapping change throughout. Earlier qualitative montages remain, and the VOC histogram is reused within Figure 14.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important weakness of v2: instance-edge claims relied mainly on downstream segmentation scores and visual examples. Direct boundary/topology evaluation, targeted design controls, and measured satellite/medical failures substantially improve validation and applicability guidance. These gains outweigh the removed code-access directions and flaws in the additions, including arithmetic inconsistencies in Tables 10/14 and a Fisher-peak argument that overlooks the varying step-size factor in Equation 16.
